wy_cedar_mountain.blurb: Cedar Mountain rises just west of Cody, Wyoming, and is almost entirely a bouldering hill, with a handful of trad lines tucked in. Problems run from V0 up to V10, with the heaviest concentration in the easy and moderate grades. The stone is sandstone, a touch softer than Joe's Valley's, so it is best left alone right after rain or snowmelt; Cody's long run of sunny days keeps that from coming up often. Aspect changes a lot across the mountain: the Stonehenge areas catch more sun, including in winter, while north-side areas like The Maze Area stay shady and cold and only work on a mild winter day. Otherwise the mountain can be climbed year-round. Cedar Mountain Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Lower Stonehenge, The Aerie and The Maze Area.

wy_main_wall_the.blurb: The Main Wall is the heart of the Wild Iris, a sport climbing crag southwest of Lander. Nearly everything is bolted, on bulging dolomite with pockets and the occasional edge, in angles from slab to horizontal roof. Routes tend to be short and bouldery for their grade. The grades start easy but centre on 5.10 to 5.12, with a good number of 5.13s and a few harder lines, so it suits a wide range of climbers. The wall faces south and takes sun most of the day, though buttresses and crevices throw shade in places. Rode Hard Wall stays cooler thanks to the trees at its base, a large roof and its concave shape, while Cowboy Poetry, a few hundred feet east, is hot and exposed. The wall is very exposed to lightning, and storms can build out of sight.

az_dry_canyon_the.blurb: The Dry is a limestone sport crag in southern Arizona, one long cliff band with several caves along it. Almost everything is bolted, and the grades centre on 5.11 and 5.12, with a fair number of 5.10s and 5.13s, a few 5.14s and very little below 5.10. The whole cliff faces due south and takes sun. Styles vary by sector: Swallow Wall, which holds the most climbs, mixes delicate faces, cracks and stemming; Bee Cave runs from steep roofs to face climbing; Superfly Sector is weighted toward 5.12 and 5.13; and Addendum Wall has short, moderate lines on sharp gray limestone that is less than vertical. Shallow End and Spine Cave add more sport lines.

az_refuge_the.blurb: The Refuge fills a valley along Upper Hackberry Creek inside Lower Devil's Canyon, part of Queen Creek Canyon in central Arizona. Trad makes up most of the climbing, with a sport minority, and the grades centre on 5.8 to 5.10 with some 5.11 and a few 5.12s. Lines were established from the ground up, with bolts only where the rock demands them, and some of the harder routes are fully bolted. Rock quality is mixed: north-facing climbs are described as superb, while some south- and west-facing ones are poor, and loose holds can remain. Sub-areas run roughly north to south from Dog Town, an east-facing wall of easy to moderate routes with morning sun, through The Torch and Faulty Towers to the Godhead areas. Raptor Ridge holds the most climbs.

co_naturita_and_paradox_valley.blurb: This is a remote stretch of western Colorado around Naturita, with no population centres nearby, so the climbing feels wide open. The rock is mostly sandstone, from short crags and pinnacles to long cracks. Sport and trad share the roped climbing, with a smaller bouldering scene, and the grades centre on 5.9 to 5.11, with a few 5.12s and boulder problems mostly at the easier end. At 16Z, a crag on a hanging valley above Big Gypsum Valley, the sandstone is highly featured, the cliff mostly faces south, wind can be strong, and the season is given as fall through spring. Big Gypsum - Dolores holds the most climbs, followed by Atomic Energy Crag, Red Rocks and 16Z.
